# pbwire Erlang binding (`bindings/erlang`)

> The Erlang/OTP binding of [pbwire](../../README.md): a C NIF over the shared C
> core. gpb generates the record definitions (`get_msg_defs/0`, or
> `get_proto_defs/0` on gpb 5+); `pbwire:load_cache/1` consumes them and
> `encode/1` / `decode/2` run in C. Same record tuples, same wire format,
> byte-identical output, ~1.6–2.4x faster than pure-Erlang gpb, with no
> libprotobuf dependency.

Facts: developed in this repo as `bindings/erlang`, license Apache-2.0 (see the
repo root). Previously published standalone; that repository is closed in favor
of this one — the API and the wire format are unchanged.
Requirements: Erlang/OTP per [`.tool-versions`](.tool-versions), a C compiler,
`make`. The NIF is compiled by a `pre_hooks` entry during `rebar3 compile`.

## Build

```shell
make erlang-test    # from the repo root: EUnit + the NIF C tests
make erlang-bench   # from the repo root: epb vs gpb (+ gpb NIF when protoc + libprotobuf exist)
```

## Docs

- [README](README.md): build, quick start, full API reference, supported protobuf features, options, benchmark table, FAQ.
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): invariants and pitfalls for agents modifying the NIF or calling the API.
- [benchmarks/README.md](benchmarks/README.md): how to reproduce the throughput numbers on `matrix3.proto`, with gpb and the gpb-NIF baseline.

## API

- `pbwire:load_cache(Module:get_msg_defs())` -> `ok`; loads/replaces the global schema cache. On gpb 5+ pass `Module:get_proto_defs()` instead (compile with `introspect_get_proto_defs`) so the proto3 markers are included.
- `pbwire:purge_cache()` -> `ok`; clears the schema.
- `pbwire:set_opts([{string_as_list, boolean()} | {with_utf8, boolean()} | {retain_cap, N} | {max_bytes, N} | {max_depth, N}])` -> `ok`; must be called before `load_cache/1`.
- `pbwire:encode(MsgRecordOrMapTuple)` -> `binary()`; raises `cache_not_exists` if no schema is loaded.
- `pbwire:decode(Binary, 'MessageName')` -> record/map tuple; raises `unknown_msg` for names missing from the schema.
- `pbwire:encode_msg(Msg, Defs)` / `pbwire:decode_msg(Bin, Name, Defs)`: load the cache on each call.
- `pbwire:encode_delimited(Msg)` / `pbwire:decode_delimited(Bin, Name)`: varint-length framed codec over the same NIF (`{Msg, Rest}` back).
- `pbwire:encode_deterministic(Msg, Defs)`: map entries sorted by key (core ordering), repeated order kept.
- JSON and text are non-goals (no second codec/loader); the conformance testee answers `skipped` for them.
- `pbwire:debug_term(Term)`: prints the internal schema term layout.

From Elixir the same calls are `:pbwire.encode/1`, `:pbwire.decode/2`, and
`:pbwire.load_cache/1` with the message atom written `:'Person'`.

## Key facts

- Supports all scalar types, enums (aliases, negative values), repeated/packed fields, nested messages, oneof, map, group, and unknown-field passthrough.
- `string` fields decode to binaries by default; `{string_as_list, true}` switches to lists. Non-Latin-1 UTF-8 requires `{with_utf8, true}` before `load_cache/1`.
- The schema cache is global to the BEAM node and shared by all processes; encode/decode take a read lock and are concurrency-safe.
- Calls run on normal schedulers (no dirty NIF); use it for normal message sizes and shard very large payload work.
- Requires gpb-generated modules (`get_msg_defs/0`, or `get_proto_defs/0` on gpb 5+) for the schema; records themselves are unchanged.
- gpb records are the generated model: there is no `codegen` output for Erlang.

- [test/ep_gpb_tests.erl](test/ep_gpb_tests.erl): byte-parity tests against gpb, useful as executable usage examples.
- [c_src/](c_src/): implementation; `src/pbwire.erl` holds the public API stubs.
